title: Letter to Emma Smith, 6 June 1832
source_note: JS, Letter, Greenville, IN, to Emma Smith, Kirtland Township, OH, 6 June 1832; handwriting and signature of JS; addressed by Newel K. Whitney; four pages; Manuscripts about Mormons at Chicago History Museum. Includes postmark, redactions, docket, and archival marking. Bifolium measuring 9¾ × 7⅞ inches (25 × 20 cm) when folded (and trimmed). JS signed the letter at the bottom of the recto side of the second leaf of the bifolium. He then closed the bifolium and turned it over, so that the verso of the second leaf became the recto of the first leaf, and added the postscript regarding the intent for Martin Harris to return with them at the top of this page (upside down in comparison with the rest of the letter). The bifolium letter was folded for mailing in double tri-fold envelope style, addressed by Whitney, and sealed with half an adhesive wafer. A docket, “Grenville June 6, 1832 | Joseph Smith Jr.,” appears at the edge of the address panel. The placement of the docket suggests the letter was initially kept folded for storage. This docket was apparently written by Willard Richards, which suggests that the letter was kept for a time in JS’s Nauvoo office. If so, the letter was eventually returned to the possession of Emma Smith, because it was found among her papers when she died. In 1880, her son Joseph Smith III donated the letter to the Chicago Historical Society (now Chicago History Museum).1 For a time, it was kept there in a scrapbook of autograph letters. The letter was attached to a leaf, which was cut short so the letter would fit within the book. The letter is also slightly trimmed, which was probably done in connection with placing it in the scrapbook. It was subsequently excised from the scrapbook, but the leaf stub is still attached to the folded edge on the back of the letter.2
